sources.title: Liviu I. Nicolaescu, Notes on the Atiyah–Singer Index Theorem, revision 15 November 2013
sources.locator: Complete Chapter 4, §§4.2–4.3.4, printed pp.139–166; Proposition 2.2.26 and its complete proof, printed pp.87–88. In §4.3.1, Definition 4.3.1, Theorem 4.3.2, Definition 4.3.3, Proposition 4.3.4 and Corollary 4.3.5; §4.3.2, Lemma 4.3.6 and Proposition 4.3.7; §4.3.3, Propositions 4.3.8–4.3.9; the final §4.3.4 heading is blank.

contents.name: Proposition 2.2.26, Weitzenböck formula and complete local proof
contents.detail: The full proof was inspected at pp.87–88. The carrier fixes the repository's skew-Hermitian Clifford and curvature conventions and gives the contraction calculation locally.

contents.name: Definition 4.3.1, heat-kernel asymptotic expansion
contents.detail: The source definition is absorbed into the carrier's uniform differentiated remainder statement; the carrier supplies a graph-norm Duhamel argument.

contents.name: Theorem 4.3.2, compact heat-kernel expansion properties
contents.detail: The source theorem and its role in the index route were read. The carrier proves the needed differentiated expansion by a local transport recursion and Duhamel estimate.

contents.name: Definition 4.3.3, approximate heat kernel
contents.detail: The approximate-kernel construction is absorbed into the explicit cutoff parametrix and recursion in the carrier.

contents.name: Proposition 4.3.4, proof deferred by the source
contents.reason: The source explicitly defers this proposition's proof and does not supply it; the assigned carrier instead proves the required Dirac graph-norm Duhamel remainder locally.

contents.name: Corollary 4.3.5, odd-dimensional index vanishing
contents.reason: The assigned theorem is the even-dimensional characteristic-form formula; no odd-dimensional index claim is needed for its statement or proof.

contents.name: Lemma 4.3.6, radial-gauge connection expansion stated without proof
contents.detail: The source states the expansion but cites another lemma for it. The carrier derives the radial-gauge identity from the curvature equation and integrates it.

contents.name: Proposition 4.3.7, Getzler order of the squared Dirac operator
contents.detail: The order calculation is used as a route check; the local carrier spells out the filtration, radial connection term and oscillator.

contents.name: Proposition 4.3.8, formal oscillator heat solution
contents.detail: The source's formal existence recursion and the carrier's finite-degree oscillator equation were compared; the carrier verifies the displayed Gaussian directly.

contents.name: Proposition 4.3.9, Mehler formula stated without proof
contents.detail: The formula is stated in the source, but no proof is attributed to it. The carrier derives the Riccati and determinant identities and checks the heat equation and normalization.

contents.name: Section 4.3.4, empty final section heading
contents.reason: The inspected PDF contains only the final section heading and no argument there, so no completion step or proof is claimed from this section.

sources.title: Konstantin Wernli, Lecture Notes on Spin Geometry, arXiv:1911.09766v1
sources.locator: §§2.3–2.4, Spin structures, Clifford modules and Dirac operators; §3.3, Lichnerowicz formula, printed pp.85–87; §4.2, Theorem 4.2.4 and twisted-spin specialization, printed pp.89–90; end of the heat-kernel proof and its rescaling-convergence footnote, p.103.

contents.name: §2.3, Spin structures and associated spinor bundles
contents.detail: Definitions and right-action conventions were read and compared. The carrier states its own realification and transition conventions.

contents.name: §2.4, Clifford modules and the geometric Dirac operator
contents.detail: The module, compatible connection and Dirac construction are represented by the local definitions; the global frame and formal-symmetry proof is supplied in the paired lemma.

contents.name: §3.3, Lichnerowicz identity
contents.detail: The theorem statement and sign convention were read. Wernli refers elsewhere for the proof; this carrier supplies the Clifford-curvature contraction.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2.4, index formula for geometric Clifford modules and its spin-twist specialization
contents.detail: The complete theorem statement and specialization were read. The local proof chain supplies the analytic domain, Fredholm, heat, Getzler and oscillator obligations.

contents.name: End of §4.2 heat proof, rescaling convergence assertion
contents.reason: The source leaves the rescaling convergence step as a sketch and cites literature; the batch does not attribute that gap to Wernli and supplies its own uniform parametrix and coefficient argument.

sources.title: Richard B. Melrose, Analysis, Loops and Spin, 2024 lecture notes
sources.locator: §1.15, Spin structures, printed pp.31–33, complete section including the good-cover transition lifts, triple-product cocycle, exactness construction, and the author's explicit remaining w2-identification and H1-torsor exercises.

contents.name: Equations (1.1.15.1)–(1.1.15.7), Spin lift and central-sign cocycle
contents.detail: The full section was inspected. The carrier adopts the transition-lift construction and proves its cocycle and sign-change calculations.

contents.name: Equation (1.1.15.9), gluing a Spin bundle from an exact sign cocycle
contents.detail: The gluing step is included and locally justified by checking the triple-overlap cocycle and the map to the fixed oriented-frame bundle.

contents.name: Identification of the obstruction with w2, left as a remaining task
contents.detail: Melrose explicitly leaves this identification open in §1.15. The carrier supplies a universal cellular obstruction comparison and checks ranks one, two and at least three.

contents.name: H1 torsor and isomorphism criterion, left as an exercise
contents.detail: The source asks the reader to verify the torsor classification. The carrier gives the sign-valued one-cocycle difference and vertex-sign isomorphism proof.
